What Are GMO Soybeans?

GMO soybeans are yellow soybeans grown from genetically modified seed varieties bred for higher yield, pest resistance, and consistent protein and oil content across large planting areas. Once harvested and cleaned, the beans are graded on protein, oil, moisture, and foreign matter before being routed to crushing plants, where they are processed into soybean meal for animal feed and crude soybean oil for further refining. On the question buyers ask most often – is Brazilian soybean GMO – the large majority of Brazil's commercial soybean crop is grown from genetically modified seed, with non-GMO identity-preserved (IP) lots supplied as a separate, lower-volume category from India on request. On GMO vs non-GMO soybean for feed, both deliver comparable protein and amino acid profiles once processed into meal; the distinction that matters most to feed buyers is typically the destination market's regulatory acceptance of GMO grain rather than a difference in nutritional value. Buyers requiring a non-GMO IP soybean India origin supplier arrangement should flag this at RFQ stage, since segregated handling, dedicated documentation, and testing add lead time and cost versus the standard GMO program described here.

What Are Non-GMO Soybeans?

Non-GMO soybeans are yellow soybeans grown from conventional, non-genetically-modified seed varieties and kept segregated from GMO grain at every stage of handling, from field collection through storage and container or vessel loading, under an identity preserved (IP) chain of custody. This segregation is what allows the beans to carry Non-GMO Project verified soybeans and identity preserved certified soybeans documentation through to the destination port. Once cleaned and sortex sorted to remove foreign matter and discolored beans, the grain is routed to food processors for soybeans for tofu wholesale, soybeans for soy milk supplier, and soybeans for natto exporter programs, or to premium feed formulators seeking a traceable, non-GMO protein source.

  • Premium and organic animal feed – identity preserved beans supplied to feed formulators requiring non-GMO or organic-adjacent inputs.

Demand for non-GMO soybeans remains concentrated among food processors in Japan, South Korea, and Europe, where tofu, soy milk, and natto manufacturers specify identity preserved beans with documented segregation from GMO handling as a standing procurement requirement. description:
More soybean oil moves across borders every year than any other vegetable oil on earth – which means a refined soybean oil supplier that can only quote one origin is one bad harvest away from letting a buyer down. France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA is built to avoid that exposure, supplying importers, re-packers, private-label bottlers, frying-oil formulators, food manufacturers and biodiesel feedstock buyers worldwide as a refined soybean oil exporter across RBD, degummed and crude grades. Our trade desk sources on a multi-origin basis from Thailand, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Indonesia and Ukraine, with origin stated on contract so no single harvest cycle or export policy can hold a programme hostage. Supply runs from 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L retail formats through to flexitank, drums and IBC tote at container scale, quoted and documented against a minimum order of 1,000 MT, across spot shipments and recurring monthly supply contracts.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Soybean oil is the world’s most widely traded vegetable oil, and refined soybean oil holds a core position across retail cooking-oil lines, industrial frying operations, food manufacturing and the biodiesel feedstock market. Demand continues to build across several fronts: refiners and industrial buyers processing further downstream, clean-label retail and food-service programmes specifying non-GMO and organic grades, buyers running their own refining capacity, and standard bulk cooking-oil bottling, deep frying and food manufacturing. France AJ sources across Thailand, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Indonesia and Ukraine, a multi-origin base that keeps a monthly contract moving when one origin’s harvest cycle, export policy or port capacity tightens, and that lets a buyer match origin to the certification and labelling requirements of the destination market.

Product Overview & Key Specifications

Refined Soybean Oil is RBD (Refined, Bleached and Deodorised) soybean oil, supplied as a commercial reference specification confirmed on each shipment’s Certificate of Analysis. Degummed (gums removed but not yet bleached or deodorised) and crude grades are also available for buyers with their own refining or biodiesel processing capacity. The two parameters that matter most to a buyer are free fatty acids (FFA) at max. 0.1% and peroxide value under 5 meq/kg: together they govern oxidative stability, which drives both shelf performance over a 12–18 month best-before window and fry-life on a production line. The smoke point of approximately 230°C places refined soybean oil among the higher-heat cooking oils, suited to deep frying and commercial high-heat cooking, while a light yellow, clear appearance is confirmed on the Certificate of Analysis, not assumed.

Industrial Applications

  • Retail & Private-Label Bottling – 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L PET formats for cooking-oil brands and re-packers
  • Deep Frying & Snack Production – deep frying and snack-line production at bulk scale, drawing on the approx. 230°C smoke point

  • Vegetable Oil Blending – blended with canola, sunflower or palm oil to meet a target specification
  • Food Service – bulk cooking-oil supply for catering, HoReCa and institutional buyers
  • Food Manufacturing – processed-food and ready-meal production as a neutral formulation oil
  • Biodiesel Feedstock – RBD, degummed and crude grades supplied in bulk to biodiesel feedstock buyers

Why Source Refined Soybean Oil from France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA

  1. Authentic product quality – FFA max. 0.1% and peroxide value under 5 meq/kg, with colour and flavour profile confirmed on each shipment’s Certificate of Analysis, never assumed.
  2. Competitive, transparent pricing – a current FOB or CIF position quoted against the world vegetable-oil market and freight at each RFQ, with no fixed price tied to any listing.
  3. Flexible order quantities and MOQs – a 1,000 MT minimum order against a one-container minimum shipment, with spot cargoes and recurring monthly supply contracts equally accommodated.
  4. International shipping & logistics – flexitank, 200kg drums and IBC tote options alongside retail-ready 1L–20L packaging, moved on FOB or CIF terms to the buyer’s destination port.
  5. Strict quality control – SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection and Certificate of Analysis available on request, sourced from producers operating under internationally recognised standards including HACCP, ISO 9001 and GMP where applicable.

Packaging & Container Loading

  • 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L PET bottles / jerry cans – retail and private-label packaging for branded and private-label cooking-oil programmes.
  • Flexitank – approx. 24 MT loaded into a 20ft container, the standard format for bulk liquid soybean oil shipments.
  • 200kg drums – an alternative bulk-liquid format for buyers requiring drummed product.
  • IBC tote – intermediate bulk containers for buyers sourcing above retail scale but below full flexitank volume.
  • Shelf life is 12–18 months depending on packaging and storage; store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight and heat sources.

Step-by-Step Ordering & Inquiry Process

  1. Buyer submits an RFQ or ICPO on company letterhead, specifying grade (RBD, degummed or crude), packaging format, quantity, preferred origin and destination port.
  2. France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA returns a preliminary offer confirming the current reference FOB or CIF position and stated origin.
  3. Buyer and seller finalise and sign the sales contract covering specification, origin, Incoterms and payment structure.
  4. Buyer arranges TT, LC, DLC or SBLC as agreed in the contract terms.
  5. Refining, packing and SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection are completed ahead of loading.
  6. Shipment proceeds with full export documentation issued for customs clearance at the destination port.

Shipment, Inspection & Documentation

Each shipment is supported by SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection and a Certificate of Analysis reporting free fatty acids, peroxide value, moisture, colour and flavour profile, available on request ahead of loading. Standard export documentation includes the commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading and Certificate of Analysis, matched to the destination country’s import requirements. Product is sourced from producers operating under internationally recognised standards, including HACCP, ISO 9001 and GMP where applicable, with Kosher and Halal certification available, or as required by the destination market, subject to the nominated refinery and contract terms. Applicable certificates are supplied depending on product, origin, producer and shipment.

Request Pricing

Because soybean oil pricing tracks the world vegetable-oil market and freight on a continuous basis, our trade desk issues a current FOB or CIF price per ton against each RFQ rather than a fixed rate; buyers researching the current refined soybean oil price per ton, FOB or CIF, should request a live reference rather than rely on a published figure. Prices are indicative only and subject to destination port, quantity, packaging, freight, market conditions and final seller confirmation. Submit your grade, packaging format, quantity, preferred origin and destination port for a current reference quotation. Contact Our Sales Team and send your B2B inquiry today.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Demand for frozen chicken MDM tracks the growth of processed-meat manufacturing — nuggets, sausages, patties, frankfurters and luncheon meat — where mechanically deboned meat is the core low-cost protein and binder. Buyers searching mdm chicken, chicken mdm, mdm suppliers and frozen mechanically deboned chicken meat mix education intent with sourcing intent, so a reliable halal chicken MDM supplier must offer both clear specifications and stable monthly tonnage. France AJ consolidates that demand through direct Brazilian origination. All pricing is indicative and reference only — it moves with the world market and is subject to destination port, quantity, packaging, freight, market conditions and final seller confirmation.

What Is Mechanically Deboned Meat (MDM)?

Mechanically deboned meat (MDM) — also called mechanically separated meat and, in food labelling, MDM or chicken paste — is the fine, paste-like meat recovered from carcasses and bone-in cuts under high pressure after the primal cuts are removed. For poultry it yields a uniform pink-red chicken MDM paste used as a cost-efficient protein and binder in processed foods. MDM can also be produced from beef, pork and other poultry where applicable. It differs from hand-deboned or block-cut chicken meat: MDM is finely comminuted for emulsion and binding, whereas hand-deboned meat keeps whole muscle structure. Our halal chicken MDM is prepared from birds processed under halal slaughter requirements.

Industrial Applications

  • Chicken nuggets, patties and burgers — MDM as the base protein and binder.
  • Sausages, frankfurters and hot dogs — fine emulsion for texture and yield.
  • Luncheon meat, mortadela and canned processed meats.
  • Pet food and further-processing lines, where applicable.

  1. Industrial-grade frozen chicken MDM from a single mechanically deboned chicken exporter.
  2. Direct Brazilian origination (Netherlands, Russia and Thailand on request) with stable monthly tonnage.

Cartons load approximately 24–27 MT on a 40ft HC reefer, shipped continuously at -18°C or lower to protect paste integrity, with labelling adjusted to each destination market’s import requirements.

mainEntity.name: What is mechanically deboned meat (MDM)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mechanically deboned meat (MDM), also called mechanically separated meat or chicken paste, is the fine, paste-like meat recovered from carcasses and bone-in cuts under high pressure after the primal cuts are removed. For poultry it produces a uniform pink-red chicken MDM used as a cost-efficient protein and binder in nuggets, sausages and other processed foods. mainEntity.name: What is the difference between MDM and hand-deboned chicken?

acceptedAnswer.text: MDM is finely comminuted into a paste for emulsion and binding in processed meats, while hand-deboned or block-cut chicken keeps its whole-muscle structure and is sold as intact cuts. MDM is the lower-cost functional protein used in nuggets, sausages and frankfurters; hand-deboned meat is used where whole pieces are required.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Whole broiler chicken is one of the most widely traded frozen proteins in bulk container volumes, with steady wholesale demand from the Middle East, West and Central Africa and Asia for retail freezers, commercial rotisserie and catering. Halal slaughter is the entry ticket for most of these markets, and shipments to China additionally require plants holding GACC registration. Because a single origin can be closed overnight by an avian-influenza suspension, wholesale buyers increasingly value a multi-origin bulk halal whole chicken programme — Brazil, the Netherlands, Russia and Thailand — that keeps container supply and pricing stable across the year. CIF and per-ton wholesale reference pricing tracks the poultry market, subject to destination port, weight grade, packaging, freight, market conditions and final seller confirmation.

What Is Grade A Halal Frozen Whole Chicken?

Grade A halal frozen whole chicken is a fully eviscerated broiler, halal slaughtered, cleaned and washed with the natural skin intact and the outer epidermis/yellow membrane removed. Our commercial reference standard targets a moisture content of under 3% (a premium no-glaze finish rather than water-loaded birds), no foreign matter, no off-odours, no feather stubs, broken bones under 2% and no bruising. Weight grades are calibrated per order. These figures are commercial reference parameters; the binding specification is set out in the seller’s official offer, the halal and health certificates and the loading inspection.

Weight Grades & Where They Sell

  • 800g – 900g: value retail packs and portion-controlled catering
  • 1000g – 1100g: the volume grades for supermarket freezers and everyday retail
  • 1200g and up: commercial rotisserie, roasting and HoReCa centrepieces
  • All grades suit further processing, portioning and private-label retail lines

Why Buy Halal Whole Chicken from France AJ Alimentaire And Food Export And Import LTDA

  1. Quality real Grade A halal frozen whole chicken — fully eviscerated, cleaned broilers with a sub-3% no-glaze finish, calibrated to your weight grade shipment after shipment.
  2. Competitive prices — four origins let us quote the sharpest workable FOB or CIF number per ton on an RFQ that follows the live market, not a fixed list.
  3. Flexible order quantities — from 5 x 40ft reefer containers (24–27 MT each) up, as spot shipments or year-round monthly contracts.
  4. Shipping internationally — unbroken -18°C reefer cold chain from plant to destination, with the export file built to clear customs without delay.
  5. Quality control — birds drawn from plants operating under Halal, HACCP and ISO 22000 standards where applicable (SIF for Brazil, GACC-listed for China), with SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection and certificates available on request.

Packaging & Container Loading

France AJ supplies halal whole chicken in 20kg export cartons (typically 4 x 5kg inner layers) or IQF/block frozen, professionally packed, labelled and palletised to your requirement, with carton labels prepared to the destination’s import rules — including China customs formats where applicable. A 40ft HC reefer container loads around 24–27 MT depending on weight grade and stacking, with a minimum of 5 containers per programme. Birds pass 8 hours of controlled drainage at 1–5°C before blast freezing at -40°C and are carried at -18°C or lower, with packing details and grade counts confirmed in the official offer.

Ordering Process

  1. Send your RFQ stating weight grade, quantity (containers), packaging and destination port.
  2. Our trade desk returns a soft offer with the current FOB or CIF reference and terms.
  3. Buyer confirms with an ICPO on company letterhead.
  4. Both parties sign the sales contract.
  5. The agreed LC / DLC / SBLC is opened.
  6. Plant production and packing run, then SGS or equivalent inspects before loading.
  7. The reefer ships under cold chain and the full document set is released.

Shipment, Inspection & Documentation

As a halal animal product, the loading inspection and certificate file are central to acceptance at destination. SGS or an equivalent body can verify the cargo at the port of loading, and halal and health/veterinary certificates are issued with the shipment. The wider set — commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading, halal certificate and GACC-linked plant details for China — is assembled to match the destination’s import rules, which vary by country and are confirmed at contract stage.

Selling it whole gives a receiving plant the full yield of the steak-producing region. France AJ supplies it sourced from Brazil, the Netherlands, South Africa, and Argentina.

mainEntity.name: What is beef omasum?

acceptedAnswer.text: Beef omasum, also traded as book tripe or bible tripe, is the lining of the third chamber of the bovine stomach, recognizable by its stack of thin, leaf-like folds. It is cleaned and used in hot pot, soups, stews, and processed food manufacturing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between beef omasum and honeycomb tripe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Omasum (book tripe) comes from the third stomach chamber and has a firm, layered, leaf-like texture, while honeycomb tripe comes from the second chamber (the reticulum) and has a honeycomb-patterned surface. Buyers should confirm which cut they need at the RFQ stage, as both are commonly offered side by side.

mainEntity.name: What is book tripe used for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Book tripe is used in hot pot preparations, ethnic soups and stews, and as an input for processed and canned food manufacturing, valued for holding its structure through long cooking times.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between bleached and unbleached omasum?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bleached omasum is lighter in color and milder in aroma after processing, while unbleached omasum keeps its natural grey-brown tone and a fuller flavor favored in some markets. Either grade can be specified when requesting a quote.

What Is Beef Shin and Shank?

Shin and shank are the working muscles from the lower fore and hind leg of the animal – the shin from the front leg, the shank from the rear – both dense with connective tissue and collagen from constant movement. Cross-cut through the bone into rounds, this is the classic osso buco cut, and buyers researching osso buco cut export programs typically ask for it bone-in to keep the marrow-filled center intact; buyers wanting the whole muscle boneless for stewing, grinding, or bone broth production can request that format instead. This is also the cut behind beef shin for braising and long, beef shin shank slow cooking preparations, where low-temperature heat breaks the collagen down into gelatin, giving the cooked meat its fall-apart texture and the braising liquid a naturally thickened body – the reason the cut is a mainstay for beef shank for soups and stews, ragùs, and bone-broth manufacturing. Buyers comparing offal and muscle cuts sometimes ask how beef shank vs heel muscle differ: heel muscle is a single lean, boneless leg muscle, while shin and shank are typically supplied with the bone in and carry visibly more connective tissue and marrow.

faq.question: What is beef shank used for?

What Are Beef Ribs?

Beef ribs come from the rib section of the carcass and are traded in a few distinct formats: whole racks for slow smoking or oven roasting, English-cut short ribs (cut parallel to the bone into thick, meaty pieces), and the flanken cut (sliced across the bones into thin strips, common in Korean-style galbi and other cross-cut grilling preparations). Rib fingers – sometimes called finger meat or rib tips – are the narrow strips of meat trimmed from between the bones once the main rack is removed; they are a distinct, lower-cost cut often supplied separately for snacking, appetizer, and beef rib fingers for kebab supply lines. Because rib meat is well marbled and sits close to connective tissue, it responds well to both low-and-slow smoking and quick high-heat grilling once cut thin, which is why the category spans BBQ racks, Korean-style flanken, and skewer-ready rib fingers under one product line.

Industrial Applications

  • Korean-style grilling (galbi) – flanken-cut ribs supplied thin-sliced across the bone for Korean BBQ and similar cross-cut grilling formats.
  • Kebab & skewer processing – rib fingers supplied as a lean, stackable strip for kebab, skewer, and appetizer production.
  • Braising & slow-cooked entrées – short ribs used in braised dishes, stews, and curry preparations across foodservice menus.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Demand for halal beef ribs has broadened as Korean-style BBQ concepts and smokehouse-style restaurant formats expand across the Gulf, Southeast Asia, and Europe, alongside steady demand from traditional braising and stewing channels. Buyers increasingly request the flanken cut split out from English-cut short ribs, and rib fingers separated as their own line item, rather than buying whole racks and portioning them in-house – a split many importers now specify at the RFQ stage. Running the product across four origins lets our trade desk keep a recurring monthly allocation open for distributors even when one region tightens export volumes, which matters for buyers locked into fixed BBQ or foodservice supply contracts.

A frozen beef short ribs 24 MT container load is typical for a 40ft HC reefer, with carton labelling matched to each destination market’s import documentation requirements.

Product Overview & Key Specifications

Halal beef shoulder from France AJ Alimentaire And Food LTDA is supplied frozen and ready for container loading, with origin, grade, packaging, and freezing detail set out as commercial reference parameters below; final specifications are confirmed in the seller’s official offer and Certificate of Analysis. What Is Beef Shoulder?

Beef shoulder, known in the trade as clod or chuck and referred to as paleta in several export markets, comes from the forequarter and carries a working muscle structure with a higher share of connective tissue than the loin or rib. Supplied to beef shoulder clod Brazil halal wholesale specification, the cut is trimmed of heavy external fat and lymph nodes while retaining the collagen that breaks down into rich body during long, slow cooking. This connective-tissue structure makes shoulder the reference cut for beef shoulder for braising / stewing programs and for the dense, well-bound texture required in beef shoulder for kebab / doner production, with boneless and bone-in formats both available at the RFQ stage.

Industrial Applications

  • Kebab and doner production – shoulder meat layered or ground for doner cones and kebab skewers.
  • Braising and stewing – whole or diced shoulder for slow-cooked stews, curries, and traditional braised dishes.
  • Industrial ground beef / mince – shoulder trim ground and packed for foodservice and retail mince programs.
  • Ethnic and traditional cuisine manufacturing – shoulder supplied for regional recipes built around long-cooked, collagen-rich cuts.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Demand for halal beef shoulder continues to track growth in doner, kebab, and traditional stew manufacturing across the Gulf, Europe, and Southeast Asia, with processors increasingly specifying boneless or bone-in format and trim level at the RFQ stage rather than accepting an unspecified forequarter cut. Buyers running mince and ground beef lines are also asking for shoulder trim as a distinct order line, a request our trade desk can service from any of the four origin programs. Running the product across Brazil, the Netherlands, South Africa, and Argentina lets us keep a recurring monthly allocation open for distributors even when one region tightens export volumes, which matters for buyers locked into fixed manufacturing or foodservice supply contracts.

  5. Strict Quality Control – Batches can be independently checked by SGS or an equivalent inspector before loading, with a halal beef shoulder with certificate of analysis issued on request; documentation varies by grade, origin, producer, and shipment.

A frozen beef shoulder reefer container of 40ft HC typically carries 24–27 MT, with carton labelling matched to each destination market’s import documentation requirements.

  6. Shipping Documentation – Each container travels with the full export paperwork set – commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading, halal certificate, and veterinary or health certificate – tailored to the destination country once the sales contract is finalized.

Global Demand & Market Trends

What Is Corned Beef?

Corned beef takes its name from the coarse “corns” of rock salt historically used to cure beef before canning, a process that slow-cooks and seasons the meat until it reaches the dense, sliceable texture buyers know. Swift Premium Corned Beef follows that same cured, slow-cooked process, sealed into a 340g pull-tab can and retort-sterilised so it needs no refrigeration until opened. The halal corned beef line is prepared from cattle processed under halal slaughter requirements, giving retail, foodservice and institutional buyers a shelf-stable protein suited to long-distance export.

A parallel food-grade stream feeds milling (grits, flour, polenta) and industrial starch and glucose processing, where Non-GMO status is often a purchasing requirement. Origin matters to price and timing: Brazil and Argentina anchor the Southern Hemisphere crop and the Santos and Up-River export lanes, while India adds an alternate origin when freight or availability shifts. Product Overview & Key Specifications

GMO yellow corn (Zea mays), traded interchangeably as yellow maize, is a genetically modified grain valued for dense starch and metabolisable energy and for the natural xanthophyll pigments that colour egg yolk and poultry skin — a key reason it is sourced as yellow corn for poultry feed as well as general compound feed. We offer it at Grade 1 / US No. 2 equivalent quality for feed mills, cattle operations and industrial processing, supplied loose by yellow corn bulk vessel or in 25/50 kg bags for yellow corn bulk in container shipments. It is distinct from our separate non-GMO / food-grade yellow corn, which serves GMO-sensitive human-consumption markets. Global Demand & Market Trends

Yellow corn is the largest-traded feed grain on earth, and demand tracks poultry, layer, cattle, swine and aquaculture output across Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America. GMO yellow corn sits at the centre of that trade for two reasons: it is the dominant, vessel-scale segment — because Brazilian and Argentine crops are largely GM — and it also feeds an industrial stream into starch, glucose, sweeteners and ethanol. Feed mills sourcing new crop yellow corn around each harvest window value the xanthophyll content that many alternative grains cannot match, while India widens the shipping calendar when South American positions tighten. As a multi-origin yellow corn exporter spanning Brazil, India and Argentina, we help buyers compare a landed yellow corn CIF price for feed mills across origins rather than committing to a single supply line. Pricing is dynamic and moves with the world market; our trade desk quotes on request against live conditions.

  • Ethanol and bio-based industrial feedstock

faq.question: What is the difference between full-fat soybeans and soybean meal?
faq.answer: Full-fat soybeans retain their natural oil content and are supplied as a whole, heat-treated bean, combining protein and energy in one feed ingredient, unlike defatted soybean meal, which has the oil removed during crushing.

faq.question: Are these soybeans roasted or extruded before shipment?
faq.answer: Beans can be supplied roasted, extruded, or raw depending on the buyer's own processing capability, with the heat-treatment format confirmed at quotation stage and urease activity documented on the Certificate of Analysis.

faq.question: Which livestock and aquaculture rations are these soybeans suited for?
faq.answer: The beans are formulated into poultry, dairy cattle, swine, and aquafeed rations, supplying a concentrated protein-and-oil ingredient for high-energy diets.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity (MOQ) for export?
faq.answer: Wholesale export starts at 12,500 MT, typically shipped as a bulk vessel parcel, with bagged container loads available for smaller volumes on request.

faq.question: What packaging options are available?
faq.answer: Soybeans can be supplied loose for bulk vessel loading, or in 25kg or 50kg bags for containerized shipments, specified at RFQ stage.

faq.question: What documentation is provided with each shipment?
faq.answer: Shipments include a Certificate of Analysis covering urease activity and mycotoxin results, a phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and GMO compliance documentation, with SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection available on request.

What Is Brown Rice?

Brown rice is unpolished, whole-grain rice that has had only its outer husk removed, leaving the bran and germ layers intact — the layers that carry most of the grain’s dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals. It is available in both long-grain and short-grain forms, and includes brown jasmine and brown basmati variants that carry the aromatic character of their milled counterparts while keeping the whole-grain nutritional profile. Organic and non-GMO brown rice options are sourced on request from certified origins, meeting the growing retail and food-manufacturing demand for traceable, minimally processed grain.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Demand for parboiled rice is concentrated most heavily in West Africa — led by Nigeria, Benin, and Ghana, with further volume moving through Togo and Côte d’Ivoire — where parboiled rice is a staple household grain and IR64 parboiled rice holds a dominant share of import volume, alongside firm secondary demand from the Middle East. Parboiled rice prices track the broader rice commodity market and shift with harvest cycles, export policy, and freight rates across our five origins. What Is Parboiled Rice?

Parboiled rice, also known as converted rice or sella rice, is produced by partially boiling paddy under pressure before milling. The process drives nutrients from the bran layer into the grain, gelatinizes the starch, and hardens the kernel, giving parboiled rice a firmer texture, lower stickiness, and longer shelf life than raw white rice once cooked. IR64 parboiled rice is milled from the widely traded IR64 non-basmati varietal and typically finishes creamy-white to light-golden, while golden sella uses a longer steaming/soaking cycle to achieve a deeper amber-gold finish favoured in several West African and Middle Eastern markets. Grading follows the same broken-grain ladder used across raw rice: 5% broken is the premium specification, 25% broken is a mid-tier commercial grade for bulk staple consumption, and 100% broken is priced for industrial and feed-adjacent processing. Buyers sourcing the raw, non-parboiled IR64 equivalent should see our Long Grain White Rice page.

mainEntity.name: What is parboiled rice, and how is it different from raw or steamed rice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Parboiled rice (also called converted rice or sella rice) is paddy that has been partially boiled under pressure before milling, a process that drives nutrients from the bran into the grain and gelatinizes the starch. This produces a firmer, less-sticky grain with a longer shelf life than raw white rice, and a yellow-golden or creamy-white hue depending on the parboiling method and polish level. It differs from raw IR64 white rice, which is milled directly from paddy with no parboiling step.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between IR64 parboiled rice and golden sella parboiled rice?

acceptedAnswer.text: IR64 parboiled rice is milled from the widely traded IR64 non-basmati varietal and typically has a creamy-white to light-golden colour after parboiling. Golden sella refers to a deeper amber-gold parboiling finish, achieved with a longer steaming/soaking cycle, and is preferred in several West African and Middle Eastern markets for its distinct colour and firmer bite after cooking. Both are quoted across the same 5%, 25%, and 100% broken grade ladder.

What Is Sushi Rice?

Sushi rice is short-grain japonica rice (Oryza sativa var. japonica), distinguished from long grain and jasmine varieties by a higher amylopectin starch content that produces its signature stickiness and cohesive bite once cooked and seasoned. Koshihikari-type varietals are the premium benchmark within this category, prized for a glossy finish and slightly sweet flavor, while Calrose is a medium-grain japonica varietal grown mainly in California and Australia and widely used as a foodservice standard in Western sushi restaurants. Short-grain japonica differs from medium-grain Calrose in grain length and stickiness profile, both of which are distinct from the light, separate texture of long grain and jasmine rice. This starch structure is what allows sushi rice to bind together for nigiri, maki, and temaki formation without falling apart. Buyers sourcing a non-aromatic long grain or aromatic jasmine profile instead should see our Long Grain White Rice and Jasmine Rice pages.

mainEntity.name: What makes sushi rice different from regular long grain or jasmine rice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sushi rice is a short-grain japonica varietal (Oryza sativa var. japonica) with a higher amylopectin starch content than long grain or jasmine rice, which gives it the signature high stickiness and cohesive bite needed for nigiri, maki, and temaki formation. Long grain and jasmine varieties are bred for a light, separate texture, the opposite of what sushi preparation requires.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Koshihikari-type sushi rice and Calrose rice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Koshihikari-type sushi rice is a premium short-grain japonica varietal prized for its glossy finish, high stickiness, and slightly sweet flavor, traditionally grown in Japan. Calrose is a medium-grain japonica varietal grown mainly in California and Australia, widely used in Western sushi restaurants as a more cost-efficient substitute. Our Vietnam-origin short-grain japonica is positioned as a competitively priced alternative to both for high-volume foodservice buyers.

1121 is an extra-long grain basmati varietal prized for its exceptional elongation ratio on cooking, with an average grain length of approximately 8.35 mm before cooking. mainEntity.name: Is basmati rice only grown in India and Pakistan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Basmati is a Geographical Indication (GI) protected varietal group that can only be authentically grown in specific notified regions of India and Pakistan; no other origin can market rice as genuine basmati. Our 1121 steam basmati program is sourced exclusively from these two GI origins under one trading relationship.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between steam, sella, and raw 1121 basmati rice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Steam-treated 1121 basmati undergoes a light steaming step before milling that firms the grain and reduces breakage while keeping a bright creamy-white colour and delicate aroma. Golden sella is parboiled through a longer soak-and-steam cycle that produces a deeper amber-gold colour and even firmer texture, favoured in several Gulf biryani markets. Raw basmati is milled directly with no steaming or parboiling, giving the lightest colour and softest cooked texture. All three are quoted across the same grain-length and broken-grain specification.

1121 basmati rice is an extra-long grain basmati variety prized for its 8.35mm average grain length, which extends further on cooking, along with its characteristic aroma and fluffy, non-sticky texture. "Golden Sella" refers to the parboiling method used before milling: paddy is soaked, steamed under pressure, and dried before hulling, which gelatinises the starch and produces a lighter, golden-yellow grain colour and a softer texture once cooked. Buyers most often raise the traditional vs 1121 basmati rice comparison: 1121 is a hybrid varietal bred for extra-long grain elongation and a milder aroma at a premium price point, while Pusa basmati is a modern high-yield varietal positioned as a more affordable, everyday-use option. Traditional White Sella occupies its own position in this family: a non-hybrid, non-GMO heritage grain chosen specifically for authenticity and aroma rather than grain length or price positioning alone.

CIF Transaction Procedures

Buyers select ONE (1) of the three procedures below and reproduce the selected procedure in the ICPO. All commercial, banking, inspection, shipping and commission terms remain subject to the final mutually executed contract, applicable law, bank approval and documentary verification.

CIF Transaction Procedure 1

  1. Buyer issues ICPO on company letterhead, including buyer banking information and valid identification.
  2. Seller issues Draft Contract to Buyer. Buyer reviews, signs, seals and returns it for final endorsement.
  3. Seller issues Commercial Invoice. Buyer issues pre-advice MT799; after confirmation by Seller's bank, Buyer opens SBLC MT760 within 7 days.
  4. Seller provides preliminary POP: Irrevocable Commitment to Supply, Statement of Product Availability, Certificate of Origin and Product Passport Analysis.
  5. Seller appoints the shipping company and signs the Charter Party Agreement for transport to Buyer's final discharge port.
  6. Seller issues 2% Performance Bond alongside the Full POP documents, including applicable export, refinery, transport, storage, vessel, Bill of Lading, SGS/Q&Q and shipping documents.
  7. Shipment commences as scheduled. Upon arrival and SGS/Q&Q or equivalent inspection, Buyer's bank releases the shipment value to Seller's bank within the agreed banking terms.
  8. Seller pays intermediaries according to the executed IMFPA.

CIF Transaction Procedure 2

  1. Buyer issues Purchase Order upon receipt and acceptance of Seller's Soft Offer.
  2. Seller issues Draft Sales and Purchase Agreement Contract for Buyer's review and signing.
  3. Seller sends partial POP to Buyer via email: (a) Statement of Availability of Product; (b) Commitment to Supply; (c) Product Passport; (d) Certificate of Origin.
  4. Seller appoints and signs the Charter Party Agreement with the Buyer and shipping company. Buyer and Seller pay 50/50 to the shipping company for transporting the product to Buyer's final discharge port.
  5. Seller SWIFTs the Full POP and 2% Performance Bond to Buyer's bank. Buyer's bank SWIFTs the Irrevocable Non-Transferable Documentary Letter of Credit to Seller's bank.
  6. Shipment commences as scheduled. Upon arrival at discharge port and after SGS/Q&Q or equivalent inspection, Buyer's bank releases the total shipment value to Seller's bank within 48 hours (two banking days) by MT103.
  7. Seller pays all intermediaries involved in the transaction as per IMFPA within 48 hours.

CIF Transaction Procedure 3 — Escrow

  1. Buyer confirms the Soft Offer and issues an ICPO, preferably with BCL where applicable, to Seller.
  2. Seller issues the Draft Contract. Buyer signs and returns it. Seller/Refinery appoints an agreed escrow/security company for both parties.
  3. The escrow/security company establishes a communication channel between the parties and the bilateral escrow agreement is executed.
  4. Seller and Buyer deposit the mutually agreed security/performance deposit for the first shipment into the escrow/security account. Deposit and refund conditions are governed by the signed escrow agreement.
  5. Seller proceeds with contract legalization and logistics/shipment arrangements.
  6. After confirmation of the agreed escrow conditions, Seller issues Full Proof of Product (POP) through the agreed secure channel / bank-to-bank process.
  7. Full POP may include export authorization, Statement of Product Availability, refinery commitment, transport contract, port storage agreement, tank receipts, SGS/Q&Q report, Bill of Lading/Q88 and Charter Party Agreement, as applicable.
  8. Shipment commences as scheduled. At the discharge port, Buyer verifies the goods and releases full payment according to the executed contract and escrow terms.
  9. After successful completion, Seller pays commissions according to the IMFPA and the escrow/security company releases refundable deposits according to the escrow agreement.

Granular sulphur is a hard, dust-controlled formed product produced by granulating molten elemental sulphur recovered from sour-gas and refinery operations. Elemental sulphur underpins two of the world’s largest industrial value chains: it is the primary feedstock for sulphuric acid and phosphate-fertilizer production, and a direct fertilizer-grade sulphur input for soil sulphur correction in oilseed, cereal and pasture cultivation. Demand tracks global fertilizer consumption, phosphate and sulphuric-acid output, and industrial applications spanning mining leach circuits, rubber vulcanisation and chemical processing. With sulphur-deficient soils expanding across major agricultural regions and phosphate demand steady, granular sulphur Rotterdam origin remains a competitively priced, export-ready supply option for buyers seeking recurring monthly tonnage under CIF and FOB terms.

Ordering Process

  4. The Seller provides Proof of Product (POP) and 2% Performance Bond, and nominates transport under a Charter Party Agreement.

CIF Transaction Procedures

Buyers select ONE (1) of the three procedures below and reproduce the selected procedure in the ICPO. All commercial, banking, inspection, shipping and commission terms remain subject to the final mutually executed contract, applicable law, bank approval and documentary verification.

CIF Transaction Procedure 1

  1. Buyer issues ICPO on company letterhead, including buyer banking information and valid identification.
  2. Seller issues Draft Contract to Buyer. Buyer reviews, signs, seals and returns it for final endorsement.
  3. Seller issues Commercial Invoice. Buyer issues pre-advice MT799; after confirmation by Seller’s bank, Buyer opens SBLC MT760 within 7 days.
  4. Seller provides preliminary POP: Irrevocable Commitment to Supply, Statement of Product Availability, Certificate of Origin and Product Passport Analysis.
  5. Seller appoints the shipping company and signs the Charter Party Agreement for transport to Buyer’s final discharge port.
  6. Seller issues 2% Performance Bond alongside the Full POP documents, including applicable export, refinery, transport, storage, vessel, Bill of Lading, SGS/Q&Q and shipping documents.
  7. Shipment commences as scheduled. Upon arrival and SGS/Q&Q or equivalent inspection, Buyer’s bank releases the shipment value to Seller’s bank within the agreed banking terms.
  8. Seller pays intermediaries according to the executed IMFPA.

CIF Transaction Procedure 2

  1. Buyer issues Purchase Order upon receipt and acceptance of Seller’s Soft Offer.
  2. Seller issues Draft Sales and Purchase Agreement Contract for Buyer’s review and signing.
  3. Seller sends partial POP to Buyer via email: (a) Statement of Availability of Product; (b) Commitment to Supply; (c) Product Passport; (d) Certificate of Origin.
  4. Seller appoints and signs Charter Party Agreement with the Buyer and shipping company. Buyer and Seller pay 50/50 to the shipping company for transporting the product to Buyer’s final discharge port.
  5. Seller SWIFTs the Full POP and 2% Performance Bond to Buyer’s bank. Buyer’s bank SWIFTs the Irrevocable Non-Transferable Documentary Letter of Credit to Seller’s bank.
  6. Shipment commences as scheduled. Upon arrival at discharge port and after SGS/Q&Q or equivalent inspection, Buyer’s bank releases total shipment value to Seller’s bank within 48 hours (two banking days) by MT103.
  7. Seller pays all intermediaries involved in the transaction as per IMFPA within 48 hours.

CIF Transaction Procedure 3 — Escrow

  1. Buyer confirms the Soft Offer and issues an ICPO, preferably with BCL where applicable, to Seller.
  2. Seller issues the Draft Contract. Buyer signs and returns it. Seller/Refinery appoints an agreed escrow/security company for both parties.
  3. The escrow/security company establishes a communication channel between the parties and the bilateral escrow agreement is executed.
  4. Seller and Buyer deposit the mutually agreed security/performance deposit for the first shipment into the escrow/security account. Deposit and refund conditions are governed by the signed escrow agreement.
  5. Seller proceeds with contract legalization and logistics/shipment arrangements.
  6. After confirmation of the agreed escrow conditions, Seller issues Full Proof of Product (POP) through the agreed secure channel / bank-to-bank process.
  7. Full POP may include export authorization, Statement of Product Availability, refinery commitment, transport contract, port storage agreement, tank receipts, SGS/Q&Q report, Bill of Lading/Q88 and Charter Party Agreement, as applicable.
  8. Shipment commences as scheduled. At the discharge port, Buyer verifies the goods and releases full payment according to the executed contract and escrow terms.
  9. After successful completion, Seller pays commissions according to the IMFPA and the escrow/security company releases refundable deposits according to the escrow agreement.

IMPORTANT — BUYER INSTRUCTIONS

mainEntity.name: What is granular sulphur used for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Granular sulphur is used mainly as a feedstock for sulphuric acid and phosphate-fertilizer production, and as a direct fertilizer-grade sulphur input to correct sulphur-deficient soils in oilseed, cereal and pasture cultivation. It is also used industrially in mining leach circuits, rubber vulcanisation and chemical processing. The hard, dust-controlled granules make it well suited to bulk handling, mechanical spreading and long-distance shipping.

mainEntity.name: What is the purity and grade of your Rotterdam granular sulphur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our Rotterdam-origin granular sulphur is a fertilizer- and industrial-grade product supplied at 99.9% minimum sulphur purity (99.5% min available on request), bright yellow and free-flowing, with low moisture (0.5% max). The exact figures for each shipment — purity, moisture, ash and acidity — are confirmed on the SGS/Q&Q Certificate of Analysis and Product Passport before loading.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between granular and prilled sulphur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are elemental sulphur of the same chemical purity. Granular (formed) sulphur has harder, larger particles with high crush strength, producing less dust and caking — making it the preferred choice for bulk blending, mechanical spreading and long-distance handling. Prilled sulphur has smaller, softer particles that dissolve or react faster but generate more dust in transit. For bulk export contracts, granular sulphur is generally specified for its handling durability.

acceptedAnswer.text: We offer 25/50kg PP/PE woven bags, FIBC big bags (1000kg / 1 MT) and bulk loading in vessel. Container shipments typically carry 24–27 MT per unit, while larger contracts move by bulk vessel (Handysize/Supramax). Custom bag marking is available for distribution markets.

acceptedAnswer.text: The process begins with a Buyer ICPO, followed by a draft contract, agreed banking instruments (LC / SBLC or escrow), Proof of Product (POP) and shipment. description:
France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA is a bulk palm oil CP8 supplier and RBD palm olein CP8 exporter supplying importers, refiners, repackers, frying-oil blenders and food manufacturers worldwide. Palm Oil CP8 — RBD palm olein with a cloud point of 8°C max — is the mid-range, temperate-climate grade positioned between the more cold-stable CP6 and the tropical-standard CP10. Our trade desk supplies it from Malaysia and Indonesia, with Thailand available as a secondary origin, on spot shipments and recurring monthly supply contracts, loaded in flexitank, flexibag, ISO tank or bulk tanker/vessel — with drums, jerry cans and carton formats arranged on request — on FOB or CIF terms, from a minimum order of 1,000 MT.

Product Overview & Key Specifications

RBD Palm Olein CP8 is refined, bleached and deodorised palm oil fractionated to a defined cold-stability point, supplied as a commercial reference specification confirmed on the certificate of analysis for each shipment.

ParameterSpecification
OriginMalaysia, Indonesia (primary); Thailand or another approved origin as secondary, as confirmed in the contract
Cloud Point8°C max
Free Fatty Acids0.1% max
Iodine Value56–58 min
Moisture and Impurities0.1% max
ColourLight yellow to golden (approx. 3R max, Lovibond, per COA)
Slip Melting PointAs per COA
Shelf Life12 months (depending on storage conditions)
PackagingFlexitank, flexibag, ISO tank or bulk tanker/vessel; drums, jerry cans and cartons on request
Container LoadingApprox. 24–27 MT per 20ft container on request; exact net quantity confirmed by packaging and payload limits
Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ)1,000 MT

The parameters above are commercial reference specifications; the binding values for any shipment are those stated in the seller’s official offer, the certificate of analysis and the pre-shipment inspection documents.

What the CP8 Cloud Point Means for Your Supply Programme

CP stands for cloud point — the temperature at which an oil begins to turn cloudy as its higher-melting fractions crystallise. CP6 is the premium, most cold-stable fraction at 6°C, CP8 sits in the middle as the versatile, temperate-region grade, and CP10 is the economical, tropical-standard olein at up to 10°C. name: Refined Canola Oil
thumbnailAlt: Refined Canola Oil for bulk wholesale export in flexitank and 1L-20L retail formats, multi-origin supply | France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA
imagesAlt: Refined Canola Oil with FFA max. 0.05-0.1%, peroxide value under 2 meq/kg and 200-230°C smoke point, packed in 1L, 2L, 5L, 20L retail formats and bulk flexitank | France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA
description:
One failed peroxide-value test at the port of destination can stall an entire container of cooking oil – and with it, a production line waiting on feedstock. That is the standard buyers hold a refined canola oil supplier to, and it is the standard France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA is built around. As a refined canola oil exporter supplying importers, re-packers, private-label bottlers, frying-oil formulators and food manufacturers worldwide, our trade desk moves wholesale refined canola oil on a multi-origin basis from Thailand, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Indonesia and Ukraine – fully refined, bleached and deodorised, low-erucic-acid rapeseed oil with a mild, neutral flavour and a 200–230°C smoke point that holds up under sustained industrial frying and retail-shelf conditions alike. Whether the requirement is a single flexitank or a recurring monthly programme, supply runs from 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L retail formats through to flexitank, flexibag and bulk tankship at container and vessel scale, quoted and documented against a minimum order of 1,000 MT.

Global Demand & Market Trends

Canola – the low-erucic-acid rapeseed cultivar – is one of the world’s leading oilseed crops, and refined canola oil holds an established position across retail cooking-oil lines and industrial frying programmes on account of its neutral flavour, high smoke point and favourable fatty-acid profile. Demand continues to build across three fronts buyers are actively sourcing for: non-GMO and organic canola oil for clean-label retail and food-service programmes, high oleic canola oil for extended-fry-life industrial applications, and standard refined canola oil for bulk cooking-oil bottling, food manufacturing and biodiesel feedstock buyers. France AJ sources across Thailand, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Indonesia and Ukraine, a multi-origin base that keeps a monthly contract moving when one origin’s harvest cycle, export policy or port capacity tightens, and that lets a buyer match origin to the certification and labelling requirements of the destination market.

What Is Refined Canola Oil?

Refined Canola Oil is fully refined, bleached and deodorised canola (low-erucic-acid rapeseed) oil, supplied as a commercial reference specification confirmed on each shipment’s Certificate of Analysis. The refining route behind this specification – full refining, bleaching and deodorising, followed by winterisation – is what produces the mild, neutral flavour that lets the oil carry a recipe rather than compete with it. The two parameters that matter most to a buyer are free fatty acids at 0.05–0.1% max and peroxide value under 2 meq/kg: together they govern oxidative stability, which drives both shelf performance over a 12–18 month best-before window and fry-life on a production line. The 200–230°C smoke point places canola among the higher-heat cooking oils, suited to deep frying, sautéing and commercial high-heat cooking, while low erucic acid (under 2%) and a winterised cold-test pass keep the oil clear at refrigeration temperatures. For retail programmes, the pale yellow, clear appearance is the shelf-facing criterion and is confirmed on the Certificate of Analysis, not assumed.

Industrial Applications

  • Retail & Private-Label Bottling – 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L PET formats for cooking-oil brands and re-packers
  • Frying & Snack Production – deep frying and snack-line production, drawing on the 200–230°C smoke point; high oleic grade available for extended fry life
  • Salad Dressings & Mayonnaise – neutral-flavour base oil for emulsified condiment manufacturing
  • Bakery & Confectionery – liquid fat for batters, sponges and cake formulations
  • Margarine Manufacturing – base oil input for margarine and spread production
  • Vegetable Oil Blending – blended with sunflower, soybean or palm oil to meet a target specification
  • Food Service – bulk cooking-oil supply for catering, HoReCa and institutional buyers
  • Food Manufacturing – processed-food and ready-meal production as a neutral formulation oil
  • Biodiesel Feedstock – bulk supply for biodiesel feedstock buyers

Why Source Refined Canola Oil from France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA

  1. Authentic refinery specification – FFA max. 0.05–0.1%, peroxide value under 2 meq/kg and erucic acid under 2%, with colour and flavour profile confirmed on each shipment’s Certificate of Analysis, never assumed.
  2. Competitive, transparent pricing by RFQ – a current FOB or CIF position quoted against the world vegetable-oil market and freight, with no fixed price tied to any listing.
  3. Flexible order quantities – a 1,000 MT minimum order against a one-container minimum shipment, with spot cargoes and recurring monthly supply contracts equally accommodated.
  4. Multi-origin sourcing base – Thailand, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Indonesia and Ukraine, stated on contract, so a single origin’s harvest cycle or export policy does not interrupt a monthly programme.
  5. International shipping & logistics – flexitank, flexibag, ISO tank and bulk tankship options alongside retail-ready 1L–20L packaging, moved on FOB or CIF terms to the buyer’s destination port.
  6. Strict quality control – SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection and Certificate of Analysis available on request, sourced from producers operating under internationally recognised standards including HACCP, ISO 9001 and GMP where applicable.

Packaging & Container Loading

  • 1L, 2L, 5L and 20L PET bottles / jerry cans – retail and private-label packaging for branded and private-label cooking-oil programmes.
  • Flexitank – approx. 24–27 MT loaded into a 20ft container, the standard format for bulk liquid canola oil shipments.
  • Flexibag – an alternative flexible bulk-liquid format for container loading, arranged against buyer specification.
  • Bulk tankship / vessel – full-vessel and part-cargo shipments for buyers sourcing above container-load scale.
  • Drums and IBC tote – arranged on request where the destination market or brand requires them.
  • Shelf life is 12–18 months depending on packaging and storage; store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight and heat sources to preserve flavour neutrality and peroxide value.

Step-by-Step Ordering & Inquiry Process

  1. Buyer submits an RFQ or ICPO on company letterhead, specifying packaging format, quantity, preferred origin and destination port.
  2. France AJ Alimentaire and Food Import and Export LTDA returns a preliminary offer confirming the current reference FOB or CIF position and stated origin.
  3. Buyer and seller finalise and sign the sales contract covering specification, origin, Incoterms and payment structure.
  4. Buyer arranges TT, LC, DLC or SBLC as agreed in the contract terms.
  5. Refining, packing and SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection are completed ahead of loading.
  6. Shipment proceeds with full export documentation issued for customs clearance at the destination port.

Shipment, Inspection & Documentation

Each shipment is supported by SGS or equivalent pre-shipment inspection and a Certificate of Analysis reporting free fatty acids, peroxide value, moisture, colour and flavour profile, available on request ahead of loading. Standard export documentation includes the commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading and Certificate of Analysis, matched to the destination country’s import requirements. Product is sourced from producers operating under internationally recognised standards, including HACCP, ISO 9001 and GMP where applicable, with Kosher and Halal certification available, or as required by the destination market, subject to the nominated refinery and contract terms. Applicable certificates are supplied depending on product, origin, producer and shipment.

Request Pricing

Because canola oil pricing tracks the world vegetable-oil market and freight on a continuous basis, our trade desk issues a current FOB or CIF price per ton against each RFQ rather than a fixed rate; buyers researching refined canola oil price per ton or refined canola oil CIF price per ton should request a live reference rather than rely on a published figure. Prices are indicative only and subject to destination port, quantity, packaging, freight, market conditions and final seller confirmation. Submit your packaging format, quantity, preferred origin and destination port for a current reference quotation. Contact Our Sales Team and send your B2B inquiry today.
